newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Marubeni considers major Cambodian industry zone.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni considers major Cambodian industry zone.

text.p: Japan's Marubeni Corp is is considering a feasibility study which would be the first step in creating Cambodia's largest industrial zone.

A Marubeni delegation told Cambodian industry minister Pou Sothirak they were "very serious" about conducting a feasibility study for a proposed $120 million, 1,000 hectare zone near Sihanoukville, Cambodia's only deep-water port, Hul Lim, under-secretary of state for the ministry, said on Thursday.
A Marubeni official confirmed the Tokyo-based company was interested in conducting studies, noting the site would likely be geared toward light industry, such as garment manufacturing.
Pou Sothirak told the 16-member Marubeni delegation he was eager to start studies on development options, and pledged to speed up rezoning laws for the site as soon as possible.
The southern town of Sihanoukville is one of Cambodia's most attractive regions for foreign investors because of its inexpensive labour and accessible port.
The government has said that establishing self-contained sites near the port would address investors' concerns about security, poor power and the country's dilapidated road system.
